notes: Shared columns (pitch, s, e_min) are taken from ISO 7040 pages only; the ISO 10511 pages are used for ht / ht_min only. Thin margin: pitch, e_min, h_min and ht_min, and every cell of M30 and M36, rest on exactly three clusters - globalfastener, amesweb, fasten.it. amesweb is an engineering reference site (calculator pages that quote one scope sentence of the standard as a note), not a manufacturer or distributor; if a verifier does not accept it, what still has three clusters is s, h (max) and m_min for M4-M24 (globalfastener, fasten.it, nfgab; boltport for s and m_min) and ht for M3-M24 without M14 (globalfastener, fasten.it, mechlabgeek). mw_min is published only by GF and AW (2 clusters) and is dropped (ayafasteners.com also prints the full table, but with globalfastener's row wording - same cluster, raw/aya_iso7040.html, not counted separately). M3 is dropped because e_min 6.01 has two clusters only (GF, AW; fasten.it prints 6.1): the largest rectangle is 12 sizes x 8 columns (96 cells); the alternative 13 sizes x 7 columns without e_min (91 cells) is equally supported. fasteners.eu / torqbolt pages titled ISO 7040 / ISO 10511 say themselves 'Table according to DIN 982 / DIN 985' (h 6.3-8-9.5-11.5-14..., s 17/19/22) and are not counted. The numbers kept are those the sources give for the 1997/2012 editions; mechlabgeek notes that the current edition is ISO 10511:2025 (and globalfastener lists ISO 7040:2025 without a public table) - no public HTML table of the 2025 editions was found, so a change in 2025 cannot be excluded. schrauben-lexikon (and its boltport copy) give h max. of the thin type only, with wrong numbers for M14 (11.23) and shifted values from M18 on - not decisive for any kept cell. fasten.it prints e min = 6.1 for M3 on its ISO 7040 page (6.01 on GF and AW; 6.01 on fasten.it's own ISO 10511 page, which is not counted for the regular type).

verification.checks_done: Verifier re-fetched every page itself on 2026-11-11 with curl (browser UA, 2.5 s pause per host; HTTP 200 for all; globalfastener detail_400 needed one retry after a 403), wrote its own stdlib HTML table reader (vt.py, gf.py, obs.py) and counting script (count.py) without using the researcher's raw/, extracted tables or scripts. Drawings that define bare symbols (schrauben-lexikon gifs, nfgab pngs) were fetched and viewed. Lead decisions applied: amesweb (calculator) not a source; a rival value printed by 2+ independent lineages removes the row; cells of another standard printed under the target title (verified equal to that standard's table) are neither support nor rival; pages reproducing the standard's text (boltport ISO 4035) excluded. A cluster whose own pages give two different values for a cell is not counted for it. Largest rectangle (cells, then rows) chosen among column subsets that contain the drawing keys. Re-counted 12 x 8 candidate cells; kept 9 x 4; per-cell clusters in nyloc.verify.md.
